string-array.name: insight_late
string-array.item: I noticed your cycle is running a little late. Try not to worry, variations of a few days are very common due to routine changes, stress, or sleep. I\'m here keeping track of everything!
Looks like your period is taking its time. Remember that variations of up to 7 days are completely normal. Take a deep breath and give your body time. 🤍
No sign of your period yet. Stress is one of the most common causes of cycle shifts. Relax, I\'m continuing to monitor everything for you!

string-array.name: insight_late_goal_pregnancy
string-array.item: Your cycle is delayed. Since you are trying to conceive, this could be a great time to take a home pregnancy test! 🤞
Your period hasn\'t arrived on schedule. If you had intercourse during your fertile days, consider taking a pregnancy test. Wishing you the best!
The delay continues. Listen to your body: if you notice unusual symptoms and are seeking pregnancy, a home test can give you clarity. 🤍

string-array.name: insight_mens_day1
string-array.item: Hello! I logged the start of your cycle. It is completely normal to feel cramps or fatigue today because your hormones are at their lowest levels. Rest as much as you can. 💜
A new cycle begins! Your uterus is working hard today, so curled up in bed with a heating pad is 100% valid. Take gentle care of yourself.
Official Day 1. Your estrogen and progesterone levels have dipped, which explains low stamina or energy. Give yourself permission to pause!

string-array.name: insight_mens_day2
string-array.item: Second day. This is usually the heaviest flow day. Remember to stay well hydrated—water helps immensely with bloating and cramps.
Day 2. Feeling heaviness or cramping is very normal today. Listen to your body and don\'t push yourself too hard; rest is essential.
We are on day two. A warm herbal tea and comfy clothes are your best allies today. Be patient with yourself, it will soon pass!

string-array.name: insight_mens_day3
string-array.item: You should start feeling your energy gently returning. If you have sweet cravings, dark chocolate is ideal for its magnesium content.
Starting today, the strongest physical symptoms usually begin to subside. Hopefully you are feeling a bit lighter!
Day 3 underway. Your body has passed the heaviest phase of bleeding. Try some light stretches if you feel up for it.

string-array.name: insight_mens_end
string-array.item: Your period is almost ending. I hope you\'re feeling much better!
Almost bidding farewell to your period for this month. Your estrogen is preparing to climb slowly again.
Final days of bleeding! You\'ll notice your energy—both mental and physical—starting to reset.

string-array.name: insight_foli_start
string-array.item: Follicular phase! Your estrogen is beginning to rise. This is the best time of the month to start new projects or try more active workouts. Enjoy that boost!
Welcome to your follicular phase. Your mind feels sharper and your body stronger. It\'s the ideal phase to socialize and organize your week!
The springtime of your cycle has arrived 🌱. With estrogen climbing, you may feel more optimistic and resilient.

string-array.name: insight_foli_mid
string-array.item: Your energy levels should be soaring. The rise in estrogen also often gives your skin an extra natural glow.
Right in the middle of your follicular phase. Feeling a creative spark? That is your biology giving you a boost. Make the most of it!
Estrogen keeps rising and along with it, your confidence. If you have a challenging task or an important meeting, this is the perfect time!

string-array.name: insight_foli_end
string-array.item: You are in the final days of your follicular phase. Your body is gearing up for ovulation. A great time for antioxidant-rich nourishing meals.
Almost at ovulation! You may notice your cervical fluid changing, becoming clearer and stretchier.
Wrapping up the follicular phase. Estrogen is about to hit its peak. Enjoy this natural surge of vitality!

string-array.name: insight_ovu_day1
string-array.item: Your fertile window opens! You might notice subtle shifts in temperature or fluid. It is also common to feel more outgoing and communicative thanks to rising estrogen.
Ovulation is approaching. During these days your body is biologically primed to be magnetic and expressive. Enjoy this vibrant phase!
Your fertile window begins. Testosterone also has a mini-peak now, which can boost your confidence and libido.

string-array.name: insight_ovu_day2
string-array.item: You are right at your ovulatory peak. Some women feel a slight twinge on one side of their lower abdomen—it\'s totally normal.
The central day of ovulation. Your energy is at its zenith, though you might also feel slightly hyperactive. Channel that energy!
Peak estrogen at its height! Your basal metabolic rate also speeds up slightly. Listen to your body if it asks for extra fuel.

string-array.name: insight_ovu_end
string-array.item: Your fertile window is about to close. After ovulation, progesterone takes the lead and you might feel ready to slow down your pace.
Bidding farewell to ovulation. The transition toward a calmer, more introspective phase begins with the arrival of progesterone.
Ovulation has concluded. If you notice a subtle drop in energy compared to yesterday, don\'t worry—it is a completely natural hormonal shift.

string-array.name: insight_luteal_start
string-array.item: Welcome to the luteal phase! Progesterone begins to rise. It acts as a natural calmative, so if you feel a little sleepier or more grounded, that\'s your body doing its job.
The luteal phase begins—the \"autumn\" of your cycle. The perfect time to focus on deep, independent work and avoid overexertion.
Progesterone is now the dominant hormone. It is super normal if you feel like staying in and having a quieter, restorative day.

string-array.name: insight_luteal_mid
string-array.item: Mid-luteal phase. If digestion feels slightly slower, it\'s because progesterone relaxes smooth muscles, including the digestive tract. Opt for warm, easy-to-digest meals.
Midway through the luteal phase. Your basal temperature is slightly higher. Make sure you get restful sleep—your body needs recovery time.
Progesterone remains elevated. If you experience cravings, treat yourself to nourishing foods while staying kind to yourself!

string-array.name: insight_luteal_pre
string-array.item: Approaching the end of your cycle. It is very common to retain fluids or feel mood shifts. Be gentle with yourself these days and get plenty of rest.
Days leading up to your period. PMS symptoms may appear. Cutting back on caffeine and excess sodium can help if you feel bloated or anxious.
Both estrogen and progesterone are dropping, which can bring feelings of irritability. Prioritize your mental comfort today!

string-array.name: insight_luteal_end
string-array.item: Your hormones are preparing to reset the cycle. Self-care is your number one priority today. ☕
One step away from starting fresh. Your body is working through the process of shedding the endometrium. A hot bath and comfortable clothing will feel great!
Final day of the luteal phase. Listen to yourself, allow yourself to feel whatever emotions arise without judgment, and welcome the new cycle calmly.

string-array.name: insight_unknown
string-array.item: Keep logging your days so I can learn more about your cycle and provide accurate insights. Together we are building your unique health history!
I\'m still learning your body\'s unique rhythms. Remember to log when your next period begins. ✨
I don\'t have enough data yet to give you an exact hormonal prediction today. Log your symptoms and periods so I can sync with you!

string-array.name: insight_pregnancy
string-array.item: Congratulations! During pregnancy, make sure to get plenty of rest and stay well hydrated.
Your body is doing incredible work. Listen to its cues and take all the time you need.
Remember to take your prenatal vitamins and attend your regular healthcare checkups.

string-array.name: insight_ovu_goal_pregnancy
string-array.item: You are in your most fertile days! An ideal window if you are trying to conceive.
Your chances of conception are highest today and tomorrow. Make the most of these days!
Egg-white cervical fluid is an excellent sign of peak fertility. Best time to try!

Data shows that restful sleep is your strongest ally against discomfort. More sleep = less pain, according to your own records.

string-array.name: insight_corr_msg_sleep_pain_negative

Your logs show that short sleep nights coincide with higher physical discomfort. Your body needs rest to help regulate pain signals.
Did you know sleep is one of the most powerful natural pain relievers? Your data confirms it: fewer hours of sleep correspond to more pain.

string-array.name: insight_corr_msg_stress_energy_negative

string-array.name: insight_corr_msg_stress_pain_positive

I detected that stress and pain go hand-in-hand in your logs. Relaxation practices don\'t just calm your mind—they ease your body too.
A clear pattern: more stress = more physical discomfort. Your body is gently asking you to nurture your emotional well-being too. 💜

string-array.name: insight_corr_msg_sleep_energy_positive

string-array.name: insight_corr_msg_water_pain_negative

A fascinating insight from your logs: less water = more discomfort. Your body needs hydration to run comfortably. Fill up that water bottle today! 💙
